Created 62 files, ran 37 commands, and 29 more tools
I’ve written the companion as a new book for your site, delivered as one tar.gz since it’s 75 new files. It has 59 sections and 351 questions, and every question has an explanation that teaches the concept, so a reader can work through it without the book.

I checked everything with a Python script that applies the content compiler’s rules (ids, option counts, correct flags, YAML). I did not run the real .NET build, so run the content processor before you deploy.

Placement (extract at the repo root):

README.md — the only changed existing file: one new row in the Library table.
content/books/in-pursuit-of-the-traveling-salesman/ — book.yml plus 14 chapter folders, each with a chapter.yml and its sections.
No files to delete.

What’s in it:

Chapters 1–12 follow the book’s chapters and section order. Each section has learning objectives, a short explanation of the concepts, a “software terms” note, and sources (the book plus the original papers).
Questions are framed in software settings where it fits: CI job ordering as setup-cost sequencing, cache warm-up routing, ordering log templates by co-occurrence, lazy constraint generation in capacity planning, and checking a solver’s answer with a duality certificate.
Short C# snippets where they help: Euler check, nearest neighbor, 2-opt, Kruskal, double-bridge kick, the duality check, the Held–Karp algorithm, and finding disconnected pieces of an LP solution.
Quotes are checked. Book quotations are in “ ”, and a script compared them against the book’s text, which caught and fixed a few misquotes. My own paraphrases use ‘ ’ so they aren’t mistaken for quotes.
Correct-answer positions are spread evenly across a–d.
Two chapters of my own:
Chapter 13 covers what changed after the book. The theory updates are a slightly better approximation algorithm than Christofides (2020), a sharper limit on approximation, and a proof that no compact LP describes the TSP. It also has new records: UK pubs, the Netherlands, Korean bars and Gaia stars. Mona Lisa and the World tour remain unsolved; their current numbers are there too.
Chapter 14 is a review that ties the chapters together through engineering decisions.
Known weakness: the correct option is often the longest and most detailed one, so a reader can sometimes guess by length. Tightening the distractors would fix this; I can do that pass if you want.
